text:
alex: Quick alert — small-chat benchmark shows host-path p99 up ~10% after yesterday's stream shaper change. Not obvious in GPU profiles.
piper: Link?
alex: https://perf.redwood/fg/3742 (flame) — big spots in token preparse and the resequencer mallocs.
jules: Can you paste the perf snippet?
alex: ```
# perf top -p host_proc
  18.4% pretokenizer::scan
  14.1% stream::resequencer::alloc_buffer
  11.0% grpc::writev
```
sana: Ahh resequencer allocs — that's the change that introduced per-segment vectors, right?
alex: Right, PR 4599 introduced the reseq buffer to handle out-of-order fragments for long streams. Helped long-stream CPU but seems to regress short, chatty reqs.
piper: We're also seeing a kv-cache p50->p99 divergence when fragments align poorly with the 4KB slab. Small tokens keep missing the hot set.
eng-bot: perfbot: uploaded run 3742109900, compare to baseline 3739000000: host-path p99 +9.6%, kv-hit-rate -1.2%
jules: Hypothesis: extra memcpy + allocs increase request parse cost, lowering observed tokens/sec. Kernel selector then prefers small-batch kernels -> worse GPU efficiency.
sana: Two quick mitigation ideas: 1) per-connection slab reuse (avoid per-fragment allocs), 2) coalesce outgoing smallfrags for up to 1ms to allow writev aggregation.
alex: I prototyped a per-conn slab -> instant CPU drop on microbench for short requests (~7% p99). Coalesce 1ms gave another ~4% but added small variance.
piper: Do we have telemetry to detect the frag boundary crossing at 4KB? Could be used to toggle conservative behavior.
alex: We can emit a small ingress metric: frag_align_bucket (0-4k,4-8k,>8k). Use it to tag traces and kernel selector.
jules: About kernel selection: we should expose an "ingress_efficiency" feature. Simple EWMA of parse+coalesce cost per request. Feed into selector so it doesn't treat temporary host noise as workload shape.
sana: Also: avoid mid-session kernel switches. Those invalidate KV cache and cause cold-starts — expensive. Keep kernel pin for entire session or add a cool-down.
piper: Agree. Also toggle SSL_WRITEV_LIMIT to allow the stack to coalesce more. Any risks on TLS latency?
alex: Microbench showed no TLS handshake regressions. But large writes occasionally see headroom added; need to watch tail.
eng-bot: deploybot: canary for slab-reuse/coalesce pushed to canary-2 at 2026-03-21T14:12Z
jules: Can someone add a synthetic kv-flap scenario to perf-tests? We need regression tests that simulate rapid small-chunk chat traffic so KV-hotness can be measured in CI.
sana: I'll add a test fixture that emits 1-5 token messages at 100-200 qps per conn for 60s and checks kv-hit-rate and host p99.
piper: Cool. Timeline?
alex: I'll finish the slab reuse patch today, coalesce toggle tomorrow. We can canary baseline -> +wf metrics next run. Expect net p99 change -9% on small-chat bench, -3% mixed.
jules: Please also update kernel-selector doc: note that ingress_efficiency is a soft signal, not the sole decider. Add cooldown heuristics.
eng-bot: perfbot: canary metrics (3742109918): host-path p99 -8.9%, kv-hit-rate +1.1%
sana: Nice. :party_parrot:
alex: Closing for now. I'll follow up with benchmark graphs and RFC link when ready. Ping me if you see any regressions in canaries.
